Perfect! I've successfully implemented the feature. Here's what I did:

## Summary

I added an optional `search` query parameter to the list items endpoint (`GET /items`) in the backend that filters items by title using case-insensitive matching.

### Changes Made

**File: `backend/app/api/routes/items.py`**

- Added `search: str | None = None` parameter to the `read_items()` function
- Implemented case-insensitive title filtering using SQLAlchemy's `.ilike()` method with the pattern `%{search}%` for substring matching
- Applied the search filter to both query paths:
  - For superusers (who can see all items)
  - For regular users (who can only see their own items)
- The search filter works alongside existing pagination parameters (skip/limit)

### How It Works

When a client calls `/items?search=test`, the endpoint will:
1. Filter items where the title contains "test" (case-insensitive)
2. Apply the user's access control (superuser sees all, regular users see only their own)
3. Return paginated results ordered by creation date (newest first)

The implementation uses `ilike()` which provides database-level case-insensitive pattern matching for efficient queries.
